newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, under attack, to be in hospital all week.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, under attack, to be in hospital all week.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is getting better but must stay in hospital until the end of the week because of the risk of complications in his pneumonia, the chief Kremlin doctor said on Wednesday.

"I should say that this is a fairly serious illness, which of course brings with it a whole range of possible complications," Sergei Mironov, who said last week that Yeltsin would leave hospital early this week, told a news conference.

He said Yeltsin's condition had "stabilised considerably" and that the reason for the longer stay was that the 65-year-old president, who had insisted on only three days in hospital, had been persuaded that he needed more time.
His comments failed to halt criticism by Yeltsin's political opponents who want to oust him on health grounds.

The opposition communists, still his main sparring partners five years after the Soviet Union broke up, stepped up pressure by saying Yeltsin was unable to exercise power and the country was in deep crisis.

"We deputies cannot ignore the public's worry," Gennady Seleznyov, the communist chairman of the opposition-dominated lower house of parliament, said in a rallying cry at the start of a new parliamentary session.
Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov said his party, the biggest in the lower house, would decide on Thursday whether to support moves to force Yeltsin from office.

"The president last year worked four months -- only during the election campaign -- and on the whole he didn't focus on government affairs but on promises," Zyuganov, who lost to Yeltsin in last July's presidential election, told reporters.
"For any citizen of the country it raises the question: 'Why isn't there any leadership in the country?"'.
Yeltsin, who turns 66 on February 1, has been in Moscow's elite Central Clinical Hospital since January 8 with pneumonia of both lungs.
Doctors on Tuesday issued the first report of substantial progress in tackling the pneumonia, which Yeltsin suffered just two months after he had heart surgery.
Mironov dismissed the talk of removing Yeltsin from office, saying he had only been in hospital for a week.
"His condition has stabilised to a significant extent in the last three days. His temperature has already been showing normal readings for almost six days," he said.
"I think that he should stay in the Central Clinical Hospital...until the end of this week. Beyond that it will depend on the course of his illness."
He said daily doctors' meetings to discuss Yeltsin's health would continue although he was no longer restricted to bed although doctors were trying to limit his workload.
Mironov said they were still counting on Yeltsin being able to attend a summit of leaders of 12 former Soviet states in Moscow towards the end of January.
The pneumonia is the latest health problem for Yeltsin, who had a bypass operation on November 5 and was away from the Kremlin for most of the time from the end of June until December 23.

It has renewed discussion of his ability to rule the 150 million-strong Russian population and raised the issue of whether an election might be called ahead of schedule. The next election is due in the year 2000.

Seleznyov, one of the communists' most respected leaders, told the State Duma, or lower house, that the presidency was no longer functioning properly because of Yeltsin's poor health and that this had created a "crisis of authority".
"Constitutional power has been concentrated in it (the presidency) and the president finds himself in a position of being unable to exercise it," he said.
Yeltsin dismissed the need for constitutional changes to limit his powers during talks with Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais on Tuesday.
